applicabilityBasis.summary: USDz is marketed for payments and a USD peg. The disclosures describe 1:1 SPCT backing, institutional minting and redemption, and secondary swaps, but do not establish an issuer obligation to redeem for a fixed amount of national currency or a bank deposit. The monetary-value redemption obligation remains unresolved; private-credit collateral and U.S. access restrictions alone do not determine GENIUS scope.

genius.notes: Anzen Group Ltd is named as the interface operator. The terms separate the protocol from company services and disclaim being party to transactions; they do not establish the legal issuer or redemption obligor of USDz. The pre-sweep issuerEntity Anzen Group Ltd is retained under the strict adjudication rule because the opened sources do not establish with high confidence that its removal is more accurate. The legal token issuer and redemption obligor remain unresolved; retaining the field does not establish a regulatory authorization. BVI governing law does not establish issuer incorporation or domicile. Terms exclude U.S. persons and attribute the no-regulatory-registration statement to the interface company. Public docs describe institutional redemption without publishing a fixed national-currency redemption obligation. Reserve disclosure is issuer-reported SPCT backing, not an independent monthly attestation. The dashboard yielded an app shell; dedicated browser navigation timed out. The reserve link in the docs, rwa.anzen.finance/transparency, did not resolve. No reserve amounts were independently verified. GENIUS issuer rules remain proposed in the opened October review sources; the Treasury SCRC procedural rule does not authorize Anzen.
